hints: Read the cumulative frequency at length 24 cm from the vertical axis (approximately 156 leaves).
Read the cumulative frequency at length 14 cm from the vertical axis (approximately 55 leaves).
walkthrough:
Read the cumulative frequency corresponding to 24 cm from the graph:
$$\text{Cumulative frequency at } 24\text{ cm} = 156$$

Read the cumulative frequency corresponding to 14 cm from the graph:
$$\text{Cumulative frequency at } 14\text{ cm} = 55$$

Subtract to find the number of leaves between 14 and 24 cm:
$$\text{Estimated count} = 156 - 55 = 99 \text{ leaves}$$

ai_rubric.Reading Cumulative-Frequency Graphs: Reads cumulative frequencies at 24 cm and 14 cm and subtracts to obtain 99 leaves (accept 98 to 100).

teacher_walkthrough: We need to estimate how many of the 160 leaves have lengths between 14 cm and 24 cm using the cumulative frequency curve.

Step 1: Read the cumulative frequency at length $24\text{ cm}$ on the horizontal axis:
Moving up to the curve and across to the vertical axis gives a cumulative frequency of $156$.

Step 2: Read the cumulative frequency at length $14\text{ cm}$ on the horizontal axis:
Moving up to the curve and across to the vertical axis gives a cumulative frequency of $55$.

Step 3: Subtract the two readings to find the number of leaves in the interval:
$$156 - 55 = 99\text{ leaves}$$
(Any value in the accepted exam range of $98$ to $100$ is fully creditworthy).

hints: If 10% of leaves have length $L$ or more, then 90% of leaves have length less than $L$.
Find 144 on the vertical cumulative frequency axis and read across and down to find the corresponding length $L$.
walkthrough:
Identify the cumulative frequency corresponding to the 90th percentile (since 10% are $L$ cm or more):
$$\text{Cumulative frequency} = 0.90 \times 160 = 144$$

Read the horizontal value corresponding to a cumulative frequency of 144 from the graph:
$$L = 22\text{ cm}$$

ai_rubric.Reading Cumulative-Frequency Graphs: Identifies 90% of 160 is 144 and reads L = 22 cm from graph.

teacher_walkthrough: We are given that 10% of the palm leaves have a length of $L\text{ cm}$ or more.

Step 1: Calculate the cumulative frequency up to length $L$:
If $10\%$ of leaves are at or above $L$, then the remaining $90\%$ must have lengths strictly less than $L$:
$$0.90 \times 160 = 144\text{ leaves}$$

Step 2: Read the length from the cumulative frequency graph:
Locate $144$ on the vertical axis, trace horizontally to intersect the cumulative frequency curve, and read down to the horizontal length axis:
$$L = 22\text{ cm}$$

hints: Find the median at cumulative frequency $0.50 \times 160 = 80$: read the horizontal length value (approximately $15.6\text{ cm}$).
Find the lower quartile $Q_1$ at cumulative frequency $0.25 \times 160 = 40$ (approximately $12.7\text{ cm}$).
Find the upper quartile $Q_3$ at cumulative frequency $0.75 \times 160 = 120$ (approximately $18.8\text{ cm}$).
Calculate the interquartile range: $\mathrm{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 18.8 - 12.7$.
walkthrough:
Read the median at cumulative frequency 80 (50% of 160):
$$\text{Median} \approx 15.6\text{ cm}$$

Read the lower and upper quartiles from the graph:
$$\text{Lower quartile } (Q_1) \text{ at cumulative frequency } 40 \approx 12.7\text{ cm}$$
$$\text{Upper quartile } (Q_3) \text{ at cumulative frequency } 120 \approx 18.8\text{ cm}$$

Calculate the interquartile range:
$$\mathrm{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 18.8 - 12.7 = 6.1\text{ cm}$$

ai_rubric.Finding Medians and Quartiles: Estimates median = 15.6 cm, quartiles 18.8 and 12.7, and calculates IQR = 6.1 cm.

teacher_walkthrough: We determine the median and interquartile range from the cumulative frequency graph of $160$ leaves.

Step 1: Estimate the median:
The median corresponds to the $50\%$ position:
$$\frac{160}{2} = 80$$
Reading across from $80$ on the vertical axis gives:
$$\text{Median} = 15.6\text{ cm}$$
(Any value in $15.5 < \text{median} < 15.8$ is accepted).

Step 2: Estimate the lower quartile ($Q_1$):
$Q_1$ corresponds to the $25\%$ position:
$$0.25 \times 160 = 40$$
Reading across from $40$ gives $Q_1 = 12.7\text{ cm}$ (accept $12.5$ to $13.0$).

Step 3: Estimate the upper quartile ($Q_3$):
$Q_3$ corresponds to the $75\%$ position:
$$0.75 \times 160 = 120$$
Reading across from $120$ gives $Q_3 = 18.8\text{ cm}$ (accept $18.5$ to $19.0$).

Step 4: Compute the Interquartile Range:
$$\mathrm{IQR} = Q_3 - Q_1 = 18.8 - 12.7 = 6.1\text{ cm}$$

Compare spread: state explicitly that Ransha's palm leaves have a lower interquartile range (less spread / less variation) than Sharim's leaves.
walkthrough:
Compare central tendency using the medians:
$$\text{Ransha's data has a higher median length than Sharim's data, indicating generally longer leaves on average.}$$

Compare spread using the interquartile ranges:
$$\text{Ransha's data has a lower interquartile range than Sharim's data, showing that Ransha's leaf lengths have less spread and are more consistent.}$$

ai_rubric.Comparing Distributions: Compares central tendency (Ransha has higher median) and spread (Ransha has lower IQR / less spread).

teacher_walkthrough: We compare the central tendency and spread of the two leaf length datasets (Ransha and Sharim).

Step 1: Compare central tendency.
Ransha's median length ($15.6\text{ cm}$) is higher than Sharim's median length. This shows that on average, the leaves measured by Ransha are longer.

Step 2: Compare spread.
Ransha's interquartile range ($6.1\text{ cm}$) is smaller than Sharim's interquartile range. This indicates that Ransha's measurements have less variability and are more tightly clustered about the median than Sharim's data.
